summary: Defines a Relay Agent Echo Request option for DHCPv6. It lets a relay agent ask the server to echo back a list of the relay agent options it names. It is a standards-track option.

plainLanguage.summary: A helper in the middle asks the main server to repeat certain notes back so it can use them.

questions: dhcpv6 relay agent echo request option
how do relay agents get options echoed in dhcpv6
what is option code 43 in dhcpv6
how does a dhcpv6 server echo relay options
subtitle: How a DHCPv6 relay agent asks the server to hand its own options back unchanged.

tldr.problem: DHCPv6 does not require a server to echo relay agent options back, so a relay may lose options it needs to return replies to clients, especially ones the server does not recognize.
tldr.mechanism: The relay adds an Echo Request option (OPTION_ERO, code 43) to its Relay-Forward message, listing the option codes it wants echoed. The server copies those options verbatim into the Relay-Reply.
tldr.outcome: A relay agent can now reliably get back the relay options it needs, even when the server does not understand them.

today: RFC 4994 is a Proposed Standard from September 2007. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Relays Need Echoes
sections.content:
In DHCPv6 (RFC 3315), a relay agent is an intermediary that delivers DHCP messages between clients and servers. It may add relay agent options to the client message before forwarding it.

The server can use those options when deciding which addresses, delegated prefixes and configuration parameters a client gets. The relay may also need some of them later to return replies to clients efficiently.
sections.plainLanguage: A helper passes messages between you and a far-away office. The helper writes small notes on each message and may need those notes later to know where the answer goes.

sections.title: The Gap Compared with DHCPv4
sections.content:
In DHCPv4, the server generally echoes the relay agent option back verbatim in server-to-client replies (RFC 3046). DHCPv6 does not require the server to do so.

That can be a problem: the relay may need some of its options back even if the server does not recognize them. This memo adds an explicit request so the relay no longer depends on server habits.
sections.plainLanguage: In the older system the office always sent your notes back. In the newer one it did not have to, so the helper needed a way to ask.

sections.title: The Relay Agent Echo Request Option
sections.content:
The option starts with the code OPTION_ERO, which is 43, and an option-len field. After that comes a list of 16-bit requested-option-code values, one for each option the relay wants echoed.

The length is 2 times the number of requested options. The relay uses this option to tell the server which relay agent options it must echo back.
sections.plainLanguage: The request is a short shopping list of option numbers. The list says: please send back these items.

sections.title: Relay Agent and Server Behavior
sections.content:
A relay agent MAY include an Echo Request option in a Relay-Forward message. If the relay behaves differently depending on whether an option is echoed, it SHOULD NOT list that option in the Echo Request. To get non-relay options returned, the relay uses OPTION_ORO instead.

When building a Relay-Reply, the server SHOULD process the ERO after the ORO and other option processing. For each option listed, it ignores the option if it is already in the Relay-Reply, and ignores it if it was not in the received Relay-Forward. Otherwise it MUST copy the option verbatim from the Relay-Forward to the Relay-Reply, even if it does not recognize the option.
sections.plainLanguage: The server checks each item on the list. If it already sent it, or never got it, it skips it. Otherwise it copies the note back exactly.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The Echo Request option is only exchanged between relay agents and DHCPv6 servers. Section 21.1 of RFC 3315 describes how to secure messages between servers and relays, and section 23 gives general DHCPv6 security considerations.

IANA has assigned the DHCPv6 option code 43 for OPTION_ERO.
sections.plainLanguage: The request travels only between the helper and the server, so it is protected the same way their other messages are. It also got its own official number, 43.

fields.name: requested-option-code-1
fields.desc: Option code of the first requested option.

fields.name: requested-option-code-2
fields.desc: Option code of the second requested option; more may follow.
